paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates estimated Hessian trace values (scaled) as a function of adapter rank for the RTE setting. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and shows four discrete tick values (4, 16, 64, 256) spaced evenly along the axis rather than at proportional numeric distances, with no units indicated. The y-axis is labeled “Traces × 10⁻⁵ (RTE)” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0.0, 4.0, and 8.0, spanning approximately 0 to 10 on the displayed scale. A single series is drawn as a thick solid black line connecting orange square markers, with vertical black error bars at each marker. The trace starts around 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ at rank 4, decreases slightly to about 2.6 × 10⁻⁵ at rank 16, then increases to roughly 4.6–4.8 × 10⁻⁵ at rank 64, and rises further to about 6.1–6.4 × 10⁻⁵ at rank 256; the error bars are relatively small at each rank compared with the y-axis range.
